findings.reason: the sections enter the plan's chain nowhere, so the followup's own statement of the remaining work is false and a coordinator obeying it leaves both undispatched.
findings.text: `f-qwnw-002` states "Sections 29 and 31 are the plan's remaining implementable work" and carries `/reckon-build queued-work-needs-no-workaround §29 §31`, but the same edit declares `s32` and `s33` implementable at plan.html:23, so the two new sections are named by no followup and by no relationship

findings.reason: the node would test a read the system has no form of, so the assertion is unobtainable unless the section names which session's view is read (or the producer-seat/liveness record the view already exposes as `no-producer`).
findings.text: §32's done-when requires "the obligations view for that project carries one row naming the failed start and quoting the message", but obligations are per session, not per project: `obligations(project, session)` returns "every current duty owed by one coordinator session" (`reckon/crew/obligations.py:4795-4818`) and stored rows are keyed by session (`reckon/crew/station_store.py:1338-1354`); a producer start failure belongs to the project and names no session, so no project-scoped obligations view exists to carry the row

response_events.note: followup f-qwnw-003 names sections 3, 29, 31, 32 and 33 as the remaining implementable work, written at version 647

wiring-1.note: followup f-qwnw-003 names sections 3, 29, 31, 32 and 33 as the remaining implementable work, written at version 647

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon crew watch --project reckon`, the quoted wrapper log line and the `watch arming lock ... remained held for 30s; arming stopped` refusal all resolve in `reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py` (`:302`, `:328`, `:479`).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §32 and §33 each declare a negative control that binds the base revision ("names which of these four assertions fail at the base revision and quotes the log line and the launch refusal"; "quotes the bind-mount failure the same submission produces at the base revision"), and both are supported by the base code (`reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py:302-303` sends the producer's stdout/stderr to `DEVNULL`; `:328` writes only the restart-limit line). The one §32 assertion that cannot be observed is reported under `reasoning`.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both sections cite `docs/evidence/fragments/queued-work-needs-no-workaround/s32.html` and `s33.html` under the repository's evidence directory (both fragment files are new sections' own deliverables and that directory exists); §33's measured run resolves at `~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261118T063008830158-qwnw-red-file-every-path-meets-the-node-contract`.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §32 and §33 name no plan label, section number, ticket or commit in a symbol or comment they ask for.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §32's root cause matches its evidence (the wrapper nulls the producer's stderr, and the registration/lease pair is per project-and-session, `reckon/crew/follower_registration.py:44-78`), but its obligations assertion names a project-scoped read the system does not have (snapshot plan.html:345).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §32's four assertions are the one defect family of a producer that cannot start (cause lost, degenerate lease/seat, launches refused), and §33's two cases are one gate-start endpoint plus its own failure case; neither section carries a second mechanism with its own premise.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — the driving followup `f-qwnw-002` names §29 and §31 as the plan's remaining implementable work while `plan-section-declarations` declares `s32` and `s33` implementable and no followup or relationship names either of them (snapshot plan.html:23, :360).
